description: Against a real SQLite: outerFails(1) writes one row, calls inner(1) (two rows, succeeds — a savepoint), then fails: all three rows are rolled back. outerHandles(1) writes one row, calls inner(7) (two rows, then fails — its savepoint is rolled back), handles the failure (y = 0) and writes a second row: exactly those two persist. Count 2, @r = 0.
rationale: §8.9.2 F10: "An inner `!` function called inside an outer envelope runs as a nested savepoint (§19.10.6), so the outer envelope can roll back the inner's writes." §19.10.6: "its `COMMIT` releases the savepoint and its `ROLLBACK` rolls back to it, and neither commits, ends, or releases the enclosing transaction. A later `fail` or exception in the enclosing handler therefore still rolls back everything".
